messages:
jen: quick async standup — GPU lane handoff for PM shift
jen: what I did: drained 4 nodes in us-west2-azb for kernel update, confirmed node groups automatically replaced (no errors). ran `kubectl drain gpu-pool-usw2-azb -l lane=low-latency` then `terraform apply` to pick up new instance templates.
jen: blockers: one spot pool (spot-ams1-b) showed 0 capacity for p4s during drain, I opened a request with cloud to refresh quotas — ticket #CLD-872.
jen: today: will finish post-drain smoke runs and tag lanes that saw >15% queue backpressure. Also want a quick pair with leo on lane ownership mapping.

leo: thanks — saw the drain, logs looked clean. I bumped the autoscaler cooldown to 120s for that pool to avoid flapping.
leo: on the spot-ams1-b issue, quota refresh is slow lately, for workaround we can route low-priority to reserved-ams1-c. I pushed a fallback policy to staging: `routeByPolicy: [latency, reserved-fallback]`.

sam: FYI I noticed queue-simulator showed increased tail latency during the replacement window (p95 ~1.9s -> 3.4s). I left a note in the perf board. Might be worth a temporary batching tweak for small requests.

sam: I can draft a quick config: `batch.max_delay_ms=8` for low-latency lane and `batch.size=8` — should smooth spikes without hurting throughput.

maria: re: tagging, I can run the script to add `lane` and `owner` tags across all AZs. Which owners should I map for ams1? jen/leo/kai?

maria: also what SLA tier do we label the new reserved fallback as — tier2?

jen: yes mapping for ams1: leo owner for reserved pools, kai owns prewarm and canary traffic, jen on incident ops. Label fallback as tier2 for now.

kai: I'll take prewarm checks for the evening window. I'll also add a short probe to verify KV cache warm-up after node replacement — quick curl to `/health?kv_ready=true`.

kai: planning a small canary in ams1-c at 21:30 UTC. Will post results here.

provisioner-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance for us-west2-azb starts in 30m. Expected impact: brief reconnections. Autoscaling policy will respect cooldown. :information_source:

leo: small ask — can someone review my PR that wires the reserved-fallback toggle into routing? #4582. It's a 2-line change.

sam: will take a look in 20.

maria: reviewed, left one nit on comment. :thumbsup:

jen: thanks team. If we see >10% error rate during maintenance we flip emergency-route to reserved-only and escalate. Otherwise I'll close this out after the smoke run. :white_check_mark:
